summary: Clean toy-like construction, a promising ceramic courier helmet and a useful Administrator emblem. However, three everyday kits still read as contemporary casual clothing with small gadgets. The Administrator needs a stronger ceremonial silhouette, and the envoy needs a distinctly foreign android identity.
problems: The Gardener reads as a beret, sweater and trousers; the Weaver as a broad pullover with a tablet; the Apprentice as a visor, sweatshirt and backpack. Their names suggest the Future more strongly than their visible construction.

Gardener, Weaver and Apprentice converge into similar rectangular shirt-and-trouser silhouettes at stream scale. Small wrist devices, chest patches and hair additions are carrying too much of the differentiation.
Most occupational details face forward or sit beside the hands, where the elevated town camera will diminish them. Stronger shoulder, head and upper-back identifiers are needed.

The Administrator's white costume and constellation badge establish some rank, but ordinary hair and a narrow visor do not provide a grand top silhouette. The detached screens visually spill toward the envoy and have no visible attachment.
The envoy resembles a more elaborate local Courier. Its tiny repairs, orbital badge and finger strips will not establish a far-travelled android delegation at stream scale.

The Weaver's wide hips-bound upper torso reaches into the shoulder area. The Courier and envoy have rigid hip-mounted panels extending across the upper legs; these need articulation clearance rather than moving as solid slabs.
The Apprentice adds a custom hair block without hiding the original hair, producing an awkward protruding tuft rather than a controlled costume silhouette.
fix: Seed-Capsule Gardener: Replace the beret and sweater outline with a fitted segmented cultivation smock, a raised neck seal and two large seed capsules physically mounted high on the upper back. Let the rounded capsules break the shoulder silhouette from above. Enlarge the forearm capsule into a clearly attached cuff; keep its light inset broad rather than adding tiny markings. Ceramic Wrap-Tabard Courier: Retain the ceramic helmet and diagonal chest band. Give the helmet a deliberate stepped rear housing, and make the parcel a chunky hard-shell container with one broad contrasting stripe and a visible grip. Shorten the central hip flap to clear the thighs, or split its lower section into separate leg-bound panels. Habitat Memory Weaver: Narrow the central upper torso from 0.62 to roughly 0.48 and move shoulder extensions onto their respective arm bones. Replace the plain cape slab with a short, stepped data-mantle attached at the upper back, using two broad contrasting surfaces readable from above. Make the wrist device a substantial fitted interface, not the primary role identifier. Canopy Apprentice: Remove the ordinary visor-and-sweatshirt treatment. Use a cropped fitted utility shell and a folded canopy assembly attached to the backpack, rising above one shoulder with a clear hinge and broad accent face. Hide the original hair if retaining custom hair geometry. Administrator of the Shared Constellation: Keep the white ceremonial mass and constellation disc. Add a substantial three-node headframe attached at the temples and rear collar, and repeat the constellation geometry across the upper shoulders. Introduce a dark collar and broad cyan upper-cape border for separation. Replace the three detached screens with one larger console visibly mounted to an articulated shoulder bracket. Far-Orbit Patched-Tabard Envoy: Establish an unmistakable machine body with a fitted asymmetric ceramic skull, dark mechanical neck and elbow joints, and solid mechanical hand shells. Use a fixed foreign plum-and-ochre panel scheme rather than the local shirt palette. Enlarge the orbital insignia onto a shoulder or upper-back plate and consolidate tiny repairs into one bold replacement panel. Split the lower tabard for leg clearance. Test every kit walking and turning at the actual 40-degree stream camera and thumbnail size.
